title: The Indian Medical Service: A National Imperative for Healthcare That Reaches Every Citizen
content: India’s healthcare challenge is no longer simply to build institutions, but to ensure that clinical expertise reaches every citizen reliably. As a physician, I see the consequences when accurate diagnosis is separated from timely treatment by workforce shortages, fragmented referrals and unclear institutional responsibility. This editorial examines whether an Indian Medical Service (IMS) could address a gap that existing administrative structures do not consistently bridge: sustained, clinically informed coordination across district, State and national health systems. Such a service must complement, not displace, State medical services and multidisciplinary public-health cadres, while respecting constitutional responsibilities. Its legitimacy would depend on transparent recruitment, rigorous administrative training and independently measured improvements in specialist access, diagnostic turnaround, referral completion, continuity of care and financial protection. An IMS should not be established for professional prestige or bureaucratic expansion. It merits consideration only if it demonstrably converts medical capacity into genuinely accessible, equitable and accountable care.
